title: Unified API Gateway for Modular Microservices
business: A logistics coordination firm managing disparate tracking, billing, and inventory microservices.
problem: The firm faces fragmented client connectivity where external mobile applications must individually authenticate and connect to five distinct internal service endpoints, leading to complex firewall rules and inconsistent security enforcement.
solution: Implementing a reverse proxy acts as a centralized entry point that intercepts all incoming client traffic, terminates TLS connections, and forwards requests to the appropriate internal origin services based on URL path routing.
steps: Configure the reverse proxy server to listen on a single public-facing IP address and port.
Define routing rules that map incoming request paths to specific internal service backend addresses.
Implement centralized TLS termination at the proxy layer to offload encryption overhead from origin services.
Apply global request headers and security policies to all proxied traffic before forwarding to internal services.
outcome: A simplified client-facing architecture where external consumers interact with a single stable endpoint, while internal services remain isolated from direct public exposure.
limitation: The reverse proxy introduces a single point of failure and a potential bottleneck for traffic throughput; monitor this by tracking the error rate and latency of the proxy process relative to backend service health.
